title: Cookies done right
summary: Every cookie attribute is a security decision: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite, Domain, Path and expiry.

steps.title: How a cookie travels
body: The server sets a cookie with a response header, and the browser sends it back on later requests to the same site:
```text
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Set-Cookie: sid=9f2c41...; Path=/; Max-Age=28800; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax
GET /me HTTP/1.1
Cookie: sid=9f2c41...

Only `name=value` comes back in `Cookie`. The attributes after it are instructions to the browser about **where, when and to whom** the cookie may be sent, and who may read it. Get them wrong and the session id leaks.

steps.prompt: Match each attribute to what it does.
pairs: JavaScript on the page can't read the cookie
not sent on cross-site POSTs or subresource requests
the browser forgets it after an hour

steps.title: The attributes in detail
body: - **`HttpOnly`**: hides the cookie from `document.cookie`. If an attacker ever runs script on your page (XSS), they still can't read the session id and send it home. Always set it on session cookies.
- **`Secure`**: never send over plain HTTP, where anyone on the coffee-shop Wi-Fi could read it. Always set it.
- **`SameSite`**: whether the cookie goes along on requests started by *other* sites.
- `Strict`: never cross-site. Even following a link from an email arrives logged out.
- `Lax` (the browser default): sent on top-level `GET` navigations (clicking a link), not on cross-site `POST`s, iframes or images.
- `None`: always sent; requires `Secure`. Only for genuine cross-site uses such as embedded widgets.
- **`Domain`**: leave it **out**. Then the cookie is *host-only*: `app.example.com` only. `Domain=example.com` sends it to every subdomain too, including that forgotten `old-blog.example.com`.
- **`Path`**: limits which paths get the cookie. Usually `/`. It is a routing convenience, not a security boundary.
- **`Expires` / `Max-Age`**: without either, it is a *session cookie*, deleted when the browser closes (browsers that restore tabs may keep it). With them, it persists.
A cookie named with the `__Host-` prefix (`__Host-sid`) is only accepted by browsers if it has `Secure`, `Path=/` and **no** `Domain`. It locks those good choices in.

steps.prompt: Your app is `app.example.com`. The marketing site `www.example.com` is run by an agency. How should the session cookie be scoped?
options: No `Domain` attribute, so it is host-only and `www.example.com` never sees it
`Domain=example.com`, so both sites can share login
`Domain=.example.com` with a leading dot for extra safety
`Path=/app`, which keeps it away from other sites
steps.explain: Setting `Domain` *widens* the cookie to every subdomain. Any subdomain that is compromised, or simply run by someone else, would then receive your users' session ids. `Path` does not separate hosts at all.

steps.prompt: This builds a `Set-Cookie` header from a few choices. What does it print?
code: string Cookie(string name, string value, bool httpOnly, bool secure, string? sameSite, int? maxAge)
steps.explain: The session cookie has no `Max-Age`, so it lasts until the browser closes. A harmless preference like a theme may persist for a year and can be readable by JavaScript.

steps.title: Cookies in ASP.NET Core
body: You rarely write the header by hand. `HttpResponse.Cookies` does it:
```csharp
ctx.Response.Cookies.Append("sid", id, new CookieOptions
HttpOnly = true,
Secure = true,
SameSite = SameSiteMode.Lax,
Path = "/",
MaxAge = TimeSpan.FromHours(8),
That produces `Set-Cookie: sid=...; max-age=28800; path=/; secure; samesite=lax; httponly` (ASP.NET writes the attribute names in lower case, which browsers accept).
Reading is a dictionary lookup that returns `null` when the cookie is missing:
```csharp
string? id = ctx.Request.Cookies["sid"];
In a real app, `AddAuthentication().AddCookie()` and `AddSession()` do this plumbing for you. Writing it once by hand shows you what they do.

steps.prompt: Complete the cookie options for a session cookie.
steps.explain: `HttpOnly` and `Secure` are both `true`, `Lax` is a good default for SameSite, and the session cookie covers the whole site with `/`.

steps.title: Log in with a cookie
prompt: The starter has two users (`ada` / `correct horse`, `grace` / `hopper-1906`), password checking, and a `sessions` dictionary. **Run checks** starts the server and calls it.

- `POST /login` with `{"username": "ada", "password": "correct horse"}`: on success, create a session id with `RandomNumberGenerator` (at least 32 bytes), store `id -> username` in `sessions`, and set a cookie named `sid` with **HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, Path=/**. Respond `200 {"user": "ada"}`. A wrong password already answers `401`.
- `GET /me`: read the `sid` cookie. Known session -> `200 {"user": "<name>"}`. Missing or unknown -> `401`.
starter: // Demo users. Passwords are stored as PBKDF2 hashes, never as text.
var sessions = new ConcurrentDictionary<string, string>();   // session id -> username
return Results.Json(new { error = "Invalid username or password." }, statusCode: 401);
// TODO: make a session id, remember it, and send it as the "sid" cookie
// Unknown users still pay for one hash, so timing doesn't reveal which names exist.
solution: // Demo users. Passwords are stored as PBKDF2 hashes, never as text.
var sessions = new ConcurrentDictionary<string, string>();   // session id -> username
return Results.Json(new { error = "Invalid username or password." }, statusCode: 401);
if (id is null || !sessions.TryGetValue(id, out var user)) return Results.Unauthorized();
// Unknown users still pay for one hash, so timing doesn't reveal which names exist.
hints: `ctx.Response.Cookies.Append("sid", id, new CookieOptions { HttpOnly = true, Secure = true, SameSite = SameSiteMode.Lax, Path = "/" });`
template: {{CODE}}
static class DojoTests
public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
var c = NewClient(http);
await Dojo.TryAsync("Login could be checked", async () =>
var bad = await Send(c, HttpMethod.Post, "/login", null, new { username = "ada", password = "wrong" });
DojoWeb.Status("a wrong password gets 401", 401, bad);
Dojo.Eq("and no sid cookie", null, SetCookie(bad, "sid"));
var ok = await Send(c, HttpMethod.Post, "/login", null, new { username = "ada", password = "correct horse" });
DojoWeb.Status("POST /login as ada gets 200", 200, ok);
Dojo.Eq("the body names the user", "ada", DojoWeb.Prop(await DojoWeb.Json(ok), "user"));
var header = SetCookie(ok, "sid");
Dojo.Check("a sid cookie is set", header is not null, "no Set-Cookie: sid=... header");
Dojo.Check("the cookie is HttpOnly", HasAttr(header, "httponly"), header ?? "");
Dojo.Check("the cookie is Secure", HasAttr(header, "secure"), header ?? "");
Dojo.Eq("the cookie is SameSite=Lax", "lax", Attr(header, "samesite")?.ToLowerInvariant());
Dojo.Eq("the cookie has Path=/", "/", Attr(header, "path"));
Dojo.Check("the cookie has no Domain", !HasAttr(header, "domain"), header ?? "");
var sid = ValueOf(header) ?? "";
Dojo.Check("the session id is at least 32 characters", sid.Length >= 32, sid);
var me = await Send(c, HttpMethod.Get, "/me", sid);
DojoWeb.Status("GET /me with the cookie gets 200", 200, me);
Dojo.Eq("and says ada", "ada", DojoWeb.Prop(await DojoWeb.Json(me), "user"));
var sid2 = await Login(c, "grace", "hopper-1906");
Dojo.Check("grace gets a different session id", sid2 is not null && sid2 != sid, sid2 ?? "none");
Dojo.Eq("GET /me with grace's cookie says grace", "grace", DojoWeb.Prop(await DojoWeb.Json(await Send(c, HttpMethod.Get, "/me", sid2)), "user"));
await Dojo.TryAsync("Missing sessions could be checked", async () =>
DojoWeb.Status("GET /me with no cookie gets 401", 401, await Send(c, HttpMethod.Get, "/me", null));
DojoWeb.Status("GET /me with a made-up id gets 401", 401, await Send(c, HttpMethod.Get, "/me", "0000"));
static HttpClient NewClient(HttpClient http) =>
new(new HttpClientHandler { UseCookies = false, AllowAutoRedirect = false }) { BaseAddress = http.BaseAddress };
static string? SetCookie(HttpResponseMessage r, string name) =>
r.Headers.TryGetValues("Set-Cookie", out var values) ? values.FirstOrDefault(c => c.StartsWith(name + "=")) : null;
static string? ValueOf(string? header) =>
header is null ? null : header.Split(';')[0].Split('=', 2)[1];
static bool HasAttr(string? header, string attr) =>
header is not null && header.Split(';').Skip(1).Select(p => p.Trim())
.Any(p => p.Equals(attr, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) || p.StartsWith(attr + "=", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase));
static string? Attr(string? header, string attr) =>
header?.Split(';').Skip(1).Select(p => p.Trim())
.FirstOrDefault(p => p.StartsWith(attr + "=", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))?.Split('=', 2)[1];
static Task<HttpResponseMessage> Send(HttpClient c, HttpMethod method, string url, string? sid, object? body = null, string? csrf = null)
var msg = new HttpRequestMessage(method, url);
if (sid is not null) msg.Headers.Add("Cookie", "sid=" + sid);
if (csrf is not null) msg.Headers.Add("X-CSRF-Token", csrf);
if (body is not null) msg.Content = JsonContent.Create(body);
return c.SendAsync(msg);
static async Task<string?> Login(HttpClient c, string user, string password, string? oldSid = null)
var r = await Send(c, HttpMethod.Post, "/login", oldSid, new { username = user, password });
return ValueOf(SetCookie(r, "sid"));
